newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes easier in Asia, IOC buys no Dubai in tender.
newsitem.headline: Crudes easier in Asia, IOC buys no Dubai in tender.

text.p: Crude oil prices were a touch easier in Asia on Friday with most overseas traders, including those in Singapore, absent from the market due to Easter holiday, traders said.
Discussion on the physical market was light, with little trading heard done.
May cash Brent was notionally assessed at $19.50/19.60 in late Tokyo trading, down about five cents from late U.S. trading levels.
In the wet market, a Murban cargo was believed sold by a European major to Singapore.
The level of the deal was said to be at ADNOC flat or at a discount of about two cents.
Traders said that IOC bought four Suez Blend cargoes and three VLCCs of Qua Iboe in its May tender, but no Dubai cargoes were taken although the crude had been offered.
One trader said that this meant that there were probably about five Dubai cargoes remaining in the market for May.

The levels of IOC's Suez Blend awards were said to be around even to the official selling price or at a premium of about three cents. The remaining two cargoes were said to have been taken at dated Brent minus $2.50 and $2.70.
India was also believed to have taken three Qua Iboe cargoes, although the levels of the deals were not immediately available.
Thailand's Bangchak was believed not to have purchased any Oman in its May tender, although it traditionally buys the crude.
However, details of any purchases were not immediately available.
